name: fig_joule_surface_3d
title: Joule heating surface against the documented cooling power of a dilution refrigerator
question: Which combinations of excitation current and sample resistance keep the Joule heating within the documented mixing-chamber cooling power, and does the checker's verdict follow the physical boundary?
model: P = I^2 R (exact) against P_cool(T_doc) of the joule_heating_vs_cooling_power model; analytic boundary I = sqrt(P_cool / R).
data: 330 Lean checks (check_batch, 1.0 s) for bluefors_ld400_hdw at T_op = 20 mK and 100 mK on a 11 x 15 (I, R) grid; cooling power 12 uW @ 20 mK and 400 uW @ 100 mK from data/cryostats/bluefors_ld.json. paper/data/fig_joule_surface_3d.json.
caption: The surface is the Joule power P = I^2R over current and sample resistance (log axes), coloured by the margin to the documented cooling power of a Bluefors LD400 at 20 mK (a) and 100 mK (b), which is drawn as a horizontal plane. The black curve is the analytic intersection I^2R = P_cool (model overlay, projected on the floor). Markers are Lean checker verdicts of the Joule coupled model at sampled (I, R) points; all 330 of 330 sampled verdicts agree with the analytic boundary.
